verdicts.reason: Quote states one-to-one mapping of APB transfer to TL-UL request and response to APB completion; testable by scenario. Actor 'system' is acceptable.

Quote states early launch from flip-flops in first APB access cycle; the actor is the bridge, not a slave generally. Checkable every cycle from interface signals (TL-UL a_valid asserted in first access cycle), so assertion is appropriate. Actor should be the bridge/system.
Registered outputs are an internal implementation/structural property, not observable from interface signals; no behaviour to check by assertion or scenario (design goal description).

Exclusions list out-of-scope features; not supporting them is not a behavioural obligation, but the bridge should not issue bursts/multiple outstanding requests; actor should be the bridge. Quote says excluded, so MUST_NOT is plausible; the check is assertion for single outstanding request.
Feature table row states APB4 full-strobe write maps to TL-UL PutFullData; Required.
Feature table row states APB4 read maps to TL-UL Get; Required.
Feature row requires local error response for unsupported strobe or misaligned address; Required.
Feature row requires TL-UL response checking and error mapping to PSLVERR; Required.
Feature row requires back-to-back APB transfers with PSEL held high; Required.

questions.question: Does 'early launch' mean TL-UL a_valid is asserted in the very first APB access cycle (PENABLE=1) or in the setup cycle registered so it is visible at access? Exact cycle must be defined.
What is the exact error response behaviour (PSLVERR timing, whether a TL-UL request is suppressed) for unsupported PSTRB or misaligned address, given partial writes are excluded?
